command: scripts/synth-soc.sh (x2: unmodified origin/main @ 4d17473, then this commit's tree); verification/tools/lint_rtl.sh (default and SRAM_MACRO_V forms); make -C verification soc-gate; make -C verification xbar periph soc boot
note: Resynthesis for issue #161: obi_xbar declared i_be_i/i_wdata_i but never read either (the decode forces every instruction-manager write to the error responder on i_we_i alone), soc_fabric only passed them through, and soc_top tied them to 4'hF / 32'h0 -- synthesis realized those constants as 36 dedicated sky130_fd_sc_hd__conb_1 tie cells (4 HI driving the i_be_i bits + 32 LO driving the i_wdata_i bits, each net exclusive to its port; verified against the baseline netlist's .i_be_i/.i_wdata_i concatenations). i_we_i, the read reachability check, is kept. synth_result.json is this commit's klt output; synth_result_baseline.json is the unmodified-main run's, kept so the before figures are auditable rather than asserted. The baseline netlist reproduced main's committed one byte-for-byte (sha256 ba018bda...), and both runs used TMPDIR unset -- klt synthesize deadlocks in Yosys' abc pass on this host under the loom sandbox TMPDIR (filed at 2AMLogic/klayout-tools); every committed netlist was produced that way.

supersedes.note: records/soc-sta-preroute/ and records/soc-pnr/ bind that netlist and so describe a netlist one change old. The change is strictly tie-cell-removing (combinational only: sequential_area_um2 is identical at 70829.1808, and the i_be_i/i_wdata_i ports no longer exist on soc_top), so no recorded timing claim moves in the unsafe direction, but re-running pre-route STA and P&R on the current netlist is outstanding work, not covered here.
